defect: learner/features_graph.build() stamped `"source": str(edge_source())` -- the module default or env override -- and IGNORED the `edges_path` it was handed.
how_it_surfaced: W4b_companyworld_rerun_run01.json ran three arms over three different edge sets and all three graph_receipts named the SAME file.

pooled.actual_source: a concatenation of BOTH files, which is neither

why_it_matters: only `source_rows` disagreed. A reader checking provenance would have been told that the never-seen 1999-2013 tape came from the 2014-2024 file it was being tested against -- i.e. would have been told the experiment did not exist. The FINDING survives (the row counts and coverage windows are right and internally consistent); the provenance line did not.

fix.code: learner/features_graph.py -- the receipt records `edges_path` when one is given, and carries `source_is_the_module_default` so 'the default' and 'a path that happens to match' are distinguishable
fix.red_proof: the fix was temporarily reverted to `str(edge_source())` and the test FAILED with `WindowsPath('C:/Users/mrthn/Aegis module/runs/MARKET-GRAPH-1/edge_instances.parquet')` against the temp fixture path; the file was restored byte-identical afterwards (grep SABOTAGE -> 0)

NOT_FIXED_reported_only: the pooled arm's scope line reads '27 of 26 panel years' -- features_graph's coverage counter includes a 2025-01 feature month beyond the panel's end, so a counter can exceed its own denominator. Cosmetic, and left for its owner.
receipts_NOT_reissued: W4b_companyworld_rerun_run01.json still carries the wrong source strings; re-running it costs a full three-arm pass and the numbers would not change. The defect and the correction are recorded here instead, and the fix is in the code that writes the next one.
